column1: # Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury: the docked canvas is one 64-bit value holding two
# floats, {1920.0f, 1080.0f}, built as movz x8,#0x44f00000 / movk x8,#0x4487,lsl #48 and
# handed to the agl display init (0x40b89c -> 0x711a80). The init stores it at display
# +0x110/+0x114, which is the +8/+0xc of the window sub-object at display+0x108, and the
# swap-chain builder (0x719970) converts exactly that pair with fcvtzu for
# nvnTextureBuilderSetSize2D. The same canvas as ints sits in the display config
# (movz x28,#0x780 / movk x28,#0x438,lsl#32 at 0x40b818). Heights only: 1080 -> 1350.
# 3D World: canvas (0x40b890, 0x40b81c) and UI-table rows below are OFF (2026-10-30). Strategy change: keep the game's 1920x1080 canvas,
# give the camera the drawable ratio (duo/research/games.tsv sites), present Stretch. See duo/design/aspect.md. The UI rows are kept for the UI step.

column1: # Super Mario Bros. Wonder: the same lever, one site. The docked canvas is the same 64-bit
# {1920.0f, 1080.0f} pair (movz x8,#0x44f00000 / movk x8,#0x4487,lsl #48) stored into the
# display config record at +0x44; the display init at 0x5a7908 takes an 8-byte size pair as
# its third argument and keeps it at display+0xf8. Heights only: 1080 -> 1350.
# Wonder canvas rows OFF (2026-10-30): the camera route replaces them (duo/design/aspect.md). Kept for reference.
# Super Mario Bros. Wonder: the window's swap chain is built from the int pair nnMain hands
# the display, not from the float pair above. nnMain (0x5a48d0) fills a 0x50-byte config block
# on its stack: 0x5a49c4 movk x8,#0x780,lsl #32 -> cfg+0x14 = 1920, 0x5a49d0 mov w8,#0x438 ->
# 0x5a49d4 stur w8,[x29,#-0x60] -> cfg+0x18 = 1080. The display ctor copies that block to
# display+0x88 (0x5a5a9c str x8,[x0],#0x88; 0x5a5aa4 memcpy(display+0x88, cfg, 0x50)), so
# display+0x9c/+0xa0 = 1920/1080; the display init 0x5a7908 reads it back (0x5a7e28
# ldp s0,s1,[x19,#0x9c], ucvtf, str into the window record's +8/+0xc) and calls the record's
# vtable slot +0x10 = 0x978a2c, which converts the same pair with fcvtzu and calls
# nvnTextureBuilderSetSize2D (0x978ae0/0x978aec) for every swap-chain texture. Heights only:
# Super Mario 3D World: the UI is nn::ui2d (lyr) layouts, and the size the layouts are drawn at
# is the game's UI resolution — the 6-entry table at 0x13e7c30, entry = {layoutW, layoutH,
# referenceW, referenceH, enum, 10 per-element values}, 0x54 bytes each. The UI resolution
# manager (ctor 0x8019a0) keeps [this+0xa58] = &entry+0x18 and its getters compute
# so at 100 % the UI resolution is entry{W,H}. The canvas is 1920x1350 after the two rows
# above, so a 1920x1080 UI resolution is stretched 1.25x vertically over it (the round A/B
# button discs measure 40x49 on device). Heights of every 1920x1080 entry: 1080 -> 1350, so
# the UI resolution matches the canvas and the layouts draw 1:1. Entries 1 and 2 are the
# 1422x800 and 1600x900 modes and are left alone; see duo/games/010028600EBDA000-ui.md.
# 3D World HUD experiments (2026-10-30): with the camera fixed and the 1080 canvas, neither the UI-table rows nor the GetScreenHeight
# rows changed the in-game HUD (duo/tools/hudcheck.py scores unchanged; screenshot identical). OFF; see duo/design/aspect.md §6.
